metadata.name: Formation OBS Color Palette
metadata.note: Palette extracted/approximated from the current Formation OBS visual identity and logo. Gold is the primary brand color. Contrast ratios below are computed, not guessed.

palette_overview.visual_intention: Warm, gold-accented identity for Formation OBS while keeping enterprise DMS clarity and hierarchy
palette_overview.target_users: Enterprise users, document managers, compliance officers, multi-tenant organizations
palette_overview.design_philosophy: Minimalist with clear hierarchy, gold as sole primary accent, warm neutrals instead of cool grays

background.name: Off White
background.usage: Main application background, primary content area

surface.name: White
surface.usage: Card backgrounds, panels, secondary content areas, forms, navigation surfaces

primary.name: OBS Gold
primary.usage: Logo, primary buttons, links, highlights, key accents

primary_hover.name: Deep Gold
primary_hover.usage: Hover states, active states, dark gold accents

text_main.name: Warm Charcoal
text_main.usage: Main headings, navigation, strong text, primary body content

text_muted.name: Muted Gray
text_muted.usage: Secondary labels, metadata, placeholders, disabled states

background.name: Deep Warm Black
background.usage: Main application background, primary content area

surface.name: Warm Charcoal Surface
surface.usage: Card backgrounds, panels, secondary content areas

primary.name: Bright Gold
primary.usage: Primary CTAs, active states, links, brand accent

text_muted.name: Warm Light Gray
text_muted.usage: Secondary text, helper text, disabled states

success.name: Success/Positive
success.description: Green tone for approval and positive feedback

warning.name: Warning/Caution
warning.description: Burnt amber, shifted away from primary gold so warning state stays visually distinct from the brand accent

error.name: Error/Danger
error.description: Red tone for errors and critical alerts

info.name: Info/Informational
info.usage: Informational messages, help text, neutral alerts

usage_rules.rule: OBS Gold on white text fails AA at normal size (2.72:1). Use dark text (#3F3F3A) on gold buttons, or reserve white-on-gold for large/bold text (18px+) only.
Darken in light theme, lighten in dark theme. Deep Gold (~4.39:1) is borderline AA — pair with bold/larger text when using white label.
Use surface color for cards/forms/nav. Use background (Off White) for page-level sections.
Use text_main for headings and body content. 10.59:1 on white, comfortably AAA.
Use for metadata, placeholders, disabled states. 3.48:1 on white — large text/UI only, never body copy.
Subtle warm-toned separation. Should not distract from content.
Use for completed actions, confirmations. Never as sole indicator (use icons too).
Use for validation failures, destructive actions. Never as sole indicator (use icons too).
Burnt amber, not gold, so warnings read distinct from brand primary. Never as sole indicator.
Use for informational content. Can be combined with other visual indicators.

recommendations: Never rely on color alone to convey information
Gold primary and amber warning are close in hue for protanopia/deuteranopia users — pair both with icons
Use icons, patterns, or text labels alongside colors
Test designs with colorblind simulation tools
Provide text descriptions for color-coded elements

implementation_requirements: OBS Gold (#B89A2E) does not meet AA for normal-size white text — default to dark text on gold surfaces
Color contrast must be verifiable with WCAG contrast checkers
Non-color visual indicators required for all status updates
Icons must accompany semantic color usage
Alternative text descriptions for color-coded information
Support high contrast mode for user preferences
Test with screen readers and assistive technologies

multi_tenant_considerations.tenant_override_strategy: CSS variables allow per-tenant theme injection
multi_tenant_considerations.storage_recommendation: Store tenant color overrides in database with validation
multi_tenant_considerations.recommended_approach: Use CSS custom properties with fallbacks to base palette
